mainTopic: רבא's arrow reading of the משנה, the condemned ox mixed with other oxen, and a ברייתא about a killer cow's calf, reread to fit רבא's rule about unborn calves.
overview: The גמרא challenges the earlier readings of שמואל and ריש לקיש, because neither fits רבי יוסי's remark, 'even if אבא חלפתא was among them.' רבא answers with a new reading of the משנה. Two people stand together, an arrow flies out from between them and kills someone, and since no one knows who shot it, both are exempt, even if one of them is a צדיק like רבי יוסי's father. The משנה's next case is a condemned ox mixed with ordinary oxen. The תנא קמא says all are stoned, and רבי יהודה says they are locked in a כיפה. A ברייתא about a cow that killed has the same dispute, and its unnamed view matches רבי יהודה. The ברייתא also says the cow's calf is permitted if born before the verdict. The גמרא challenges this from רבא's rule that an unborn calf gores together with its mother. It answers by rereading the ברייתא as being about whether the cow became pregnant before or after the verdict. Finally, the גמרא notes that this reading fits the view of זה וזה גורם אסור, and starts to question it according to the other view, a challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How can רבי יוסי mention his father?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the earlier readings of the משנה fit with רבי יוסי's remark, 'even if אבא חלפתא was among them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how does that fit with what is taught about this: רבי יוסי says, 'Even if אבא חלפתא was among them'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier explanations of the משנה. If the משנה is about a killer mixed with other killers, or about oxen, then רבי יוסי's comment about his own father makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל's reading, the killer is mixed with other condemned murderers, and רבי יוסי would never put his righteous father in that group. Under ריש לקיש's reading, the משנה is about oxen, and a person like אבא חלפתא has no place in that case. So the remark shows that both readings must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your explanation is right)
Is that what is taught about it? (how does that fit?)
Abba Chalafta, רבי יוסי's father, a righteous sage

steps.confusionAlert: This question is aimed at explanations given earlier on the דף (שמואל and ריש לקיש), which do not appear in this text. 'If so' points back to them.

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier explanations of the משנה by שמואל and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: is that what is taught about it:
Rabbi Yosei says:
even if Abba Chalafta was among them?
phrases.notes: אבא חלפתא was רבי יוסי's own father, a righteous sage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier explanations of the משנה (from before this text) using a ברייתא statement of רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The readings of שמואל (a murderer mixed with other murderers) and ריש לקיש (an ox mixed with other oxen).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's remark puts a righteous person in the group. That cannot fit a group of condemned murderers, and it has no meaning in a case about oxen.

steps.title: רבא: two people and a stray arrow
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the משנה as a case where an arrow flew out from between two people and killed someone. Both are exempt, even if one of them is a צדיק like אבא חלפתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This is what the משנה means. Two people were standing together, and an arrow came out from between them and killed someone. Both are exempt. And רבי יוסי said: even if אבא חלפתא was one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new reading of the משנה that fits רבי יוסי's remark. The case is about not knowing which of two people shot a deadly arrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we cannot tell which of the two shot the arrow, neither can be punished, so both are exempt. רבי יוסי's point is that this stays true even when one of the two is obviously righteous. You might think 'surely the other one did it,' but without clear testimony, nobody can be punished.
steps.whatToRemember: Under רבא's reading, if it is unclear which of two people killed, both are exempt. This holds even if one of them is a צדיק, because a guess is not enough to punish anyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that בית דין cannot punish based on probability or someone's reputation. They need clear knowledge of who did the act.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
this is what it is saying:
two who were standing,
and an arrow came out from between them and killed —
both of them are exempt.
And Rabbi Yosei said:
even if Abba Chalafta was among them.
phrases.notes: Even though we would never suspect him, we still cannot tell which of the two shot, so both go free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by replacing the earlier readings with a new case that fits רבי יוסי's remark.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה was about a murderer mixed with other murderers, or about oxen.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first case in the משנה is two people from whose midst an arrow killed someone. Both are exempt, even if one is a צדיק like אבא חלפתא.

steps.title: A condemned ox mixed with other oxen
steps.stepSummary: The משנה moves to a second case: a condemned ox mixed with ordinary oxen. The תנא קמא says all are stoned, and רבי יהודה says they are locked in a כיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And an ox whose death sentence was already decided, which got mixed with other ordinary oxen: they stone all of them. רבי יהודה says: they put them into a vaulted chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing רבא's reading, the משנה now teaches a separate case about animals. The condemned ox is mixed up with innocent oxen, and the תנאים argue about what to do with the whole group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox was already sentenced, but now we cannot tell which one it is. The first opinion stones every ox in the group. רבי יהודה does not stone them and instead has them locked away in a כיפה.

keyTerms.meaning: they gather them into a vaulted chamber

steps.confusionAlert: Under רבא, the ox case is a separate second case in the משנה. It is not the explanation of the first case, the way ריש לקיש had read it.

phrases.english: And an ox whose verdict was finalized,
that became mixed with other, ordinary oxen —
they stone them.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
they gather them into a vaulted chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשׁוֹר שֶׁנִּגְמַר דִּינוֹ, שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בִּשְׁוָורִין אֲחֵרִים מְעַלְּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's reading of the משנה by presenting its second, separate case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condemned ox mixed with ordinary oxen: the תנא קמא says all are stoned, and רבי יהודה says they are placed in a כיפה.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a cow that killed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a killer cow's calf is permitted if born before the verdict and forbidden if born after. If the cow got mixed with others, the unnamed view puts them in a כיפה, like רבי יהודה, while רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says to stone them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: A cow that killed and later gave birth: if it gave birth before its verdict was decided, the calf is permitted. If it gave birth after its verdict was decided, the calf is forbidden. If the cow got mixed with others, and those got mixed with still others, they put them in a vaulted chamber. רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says: they bring them to בית דין and stone them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that has the same argument about a mixed-up killer animal. Its unnamed opinion matches רבי יהודה in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds a new detail: the calf is tied to the mother only if it was born after the verdict. It then repeats the mixture dispute. The unnamed opinion says כיפה, like רבי יהודה, while רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says stoning, like the first opinion in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא
רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון

steps.whatToRemember: The verdict is the turning point for the calf. As the ברייתא first reads, a calf born before the verdict is permitted and one born after is forbidden; Step 6 rereads this as being about when the calf was conceived. For a mixed group of animals, the כיפה view (רבי יהודה and the unnamed ברייתא) is set against the stoning view (the first opinion in the משנה and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון).
steps.confusionAlert: 'Others mixed with others' means the mix-up spread through several groups. Even so, the two opinions stay the same: כיפה or stoning.

phrases.english: And it was taught:
a cow that killed
and afterward gave birth,

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמַר דִּינָה יָלְדָה –
phrases.english: if it gave birth before its verdict was finalized —
its offspring is permitted,
if it gave birth after its verdict was finalized —
its offspring is forbidden.
If it became mixed with others,
and the others with others —
they gather them into a vaulted chamber.
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
they bring them to court
and stone them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: פָּרָה שֶׁהֵמִיתָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ יָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with the same dispute as the ox case in the משנה. Its unnamed view sides with רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's ruling that a mixed group containing a condemned animal is placed in a כיפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An unnamed ברייתא about a cow that killed, which rules כונסין אותן לכיפה, against רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: Challenge from רבא: an unborn calf gores together with its mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's ruling that a calf born before the verdict is permitted. It then asks how this can be, since the calf was already inside the cow when she gored, and רבא says such a calf is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: if the cow gave birth before her verdict was finished, the calf is permitted. But the calf was already inside her when she gored! And רבא said that the calf of a goring cow is forbidden, because she and her calf gored together. In the same way, the calf of a cow used for bestiality is forbidden, because she and her calf were used together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back one line of the ברייתא and attacks it. It uses a rule of רבא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A calf born before the verdict was usually already in the womb when the cow gored. רבא holds that an unborn calf is part of its mother's act, so it shares her forbidden status. That makes it hard to see how the ברייתא can call this calf permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said' — the גמרא is quoting a line from a source it just brought
Her verdict was finalized (the בית דין finished judging the animal)
The calf of a cow that gored
An animal that was used for bestiality

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the calf is put to death. He is saying it is forbidden, for example to be brought as a קרבן, because it took part in its mother's act.

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמַר דִּינָה יָלְדָה,
phrases.english: If she gave birth before her verdict was finalized,
her calf is permitted.
And is that so even though when she gored
she was pregnant?
But didn't רבא say:
The calf of a goring cow is forbidden,
phrases.notes: Forbidden to be brought as a קרבן, like any animal that killed a person.

phrases.english: since she and her calf gored together;
and the calf of a cow used for bestiality is forbidden,
since she and her calf were used for bestiality together!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּכִי נְגַחָה הֲוָת מְיעַבְּרָה? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first ruling of the ברייתא brought in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a calf born before the verdict is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a calf was in the womb at the time of goring. רבא says an unborn calf shares its mother's act and is forbidden, so the ברייתא seems to contradict רבא.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא as being about when the cow became pregnant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading of the ברייתא. The case is a cow that became pregnant after the goring. The question is whether she conceived before or after the verdict.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: if she became pregnant and gave birth before her verdict was finalized, her calf is permitted. If she became pregnant and gave birth after her verdict was finalized, her calf is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the wording of the ברייתא. Now the ברייתא is about a calf conceived after the goring, not a calf that was already in the womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading the calf never took part in the goring, so רבא's rule does not apply to it. What matters now is whether the mother was already sentenced, and so forbidden, when the calf was conceived.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say' — read the source this other way

phrases.english: Say:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing the wording of the ברייתא so it does not clash with רבא.

phrases.english: If before her verdict was finalized
she became pregnant and gave birth,
her calf is permitted;
if after her verdict was finalized
she became pregnant and gave birth,
her calf is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמַר דִּינָה עִיבְּרָה וְיָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5's challenge by changing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text and changing the case (אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא talks about a calf already in the womb at the goring, which contradicts רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא talks about a calf conceived after the goring. It is permitted if conceived before the verdict and forbidden if conceived after.

steps.title: This works only for the view that two causes together make it forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new challenge. The new reading fits the opinion that when a permitted factor and a forbidden factor together produce something, the result is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says that when this and that both cause something, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא says the new reading fits one opinion, and it is getting ready to ask about the opposite opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A calf conceived after the verdict comes from two sources: a permitted bull and a forbidden cow. Calling that calf forbidden matches the view of זה וזה גורם אסור. The implied problem is the other view, which says such a result is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This works well according to the one who says' — it opens a challenge from the other opinion
'This and that cause' — a permitted factor and a forbidden factor produce something together

steps.confusionAlert: 'הניחא' sounds like a happy ending, but it is actually the first half of a question. The 'but according to the other view' part is about to come.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says:
when this and that both cause it, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Here 'this' is the permitted bull and 'that' is the forbidden cow, which together produce the calf.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם – אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer from Step 6 against a general rule about results that come from two causes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rereading in Step 6, which says a calf conceived after the verdict is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That ruling works only if זה וזה גורם אסור. The setup suggests it will fail for the opinion that זה וזה גורם is permitted.
